meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was Owen's grade changed without anyone calling me first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Text pasted into a document doesn't tell me who wrote it. You still haven't answered me: was Owen spoken to before the zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. What else do you have besides that history? I'll want all of it in an email.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Students misquote plays all the time. A wrong line costs marks, it doesn't prove who wrote the essay.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. Whatever you think this is, it stays off his record and it stays quiet. What are you proposing?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay; that's called revising. You still haven't told me what you're proposing.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine. A private rewrite, before December 1, his record clean, and I'm doing it to put this behind him. In writing tonight, and I want the zero out of the gradebook today.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
He'll be there. Put Thursday the twelfth in the email, with the time and the room.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Dear Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday, November 12, after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook and written confirmation of the time and room. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to the private supervised rewrite under 4.4, and she still wants the zero out of the gradebook and the time and room confirmed in writing; that is the fair outcome, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You showed the fabricated Hamlet line with the play open beside it, and she could check it herself, which is why her defence stopped holding.
What cost ground: You let her question about whether Owen was spoken to before the zero go unanswered twice, which kept her pressing on procedure.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its edits near midnight on October 28, came close to that night, but it proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether Owen was spoken to before the zero, answer it directly right after your apology, since 4.1 was the point she was circling.
